headline: GOLDEN CARIBOO STEP-OUT QGQ26-35 DRILLS PAST 416m — BC Halo Zone Hole Stays in Favourable Volcanic Package With No End in Sight
snippet: Golden Cariboo Resources (CSE: GCC) reported that step-out hole QGQ26-35 at the Halo Zone on its Quesnel property in British Columbia has drilled past 416 metres while remaining within the favourable volcanic package — meaning the hole has not exited the mineralizing horizon at that depth. For investors, a step-out hole of this length still inside host rock indicates the Halo Zone system extends significantly beyond its current resource boundary, adding open-pittable scale optionality to what was already one of the more watched BC gold drill programs this cycle.

headline: FOREMOST CLEAN ENERGY HITS URANIUM MINERALIZATION IN MAIDEN DRILL AT TURKEY LAKE — Saskatchewan Assays Pending; First-Pass Success in Athabasca Basin Margin
snippet: Foremost Clean Energy (TSX-V) confirmed uranium mineralization in its inaugural drill program at the Turkey Lake project in northern Saskatchewan's Athabasca Basin margin on November 17, with chemical assay results still pending. A first-pass discovery of uranium mineralization before assay confirmation is a material milestone that places Turkey Lake in the same first-drill cohort as historical basin margin discoveries that later delineated significant high-grade uranium systems — the region hosts some of the world's highest uranium grades.

headline: HOT CHILI HITS 638m AT 0.41% CuEq FROM SURFACE AT LA VERDE — Largest Single Hole to Date at Chilean Copper-Gold Porphyry
snippet: Hot Chili (TSX-V: HCH) reported diamond hole DKD086 at La Verde, Chile, returning 638 metres at 0.41% copper-equivalent from surface — the company's largest single-hole intersection to date at the porphyry copper-gold project. The result adds bulk-tonnage scale to a system already attracting major copper producer interest; remaining assays from the program are expected by late December 2026, meaning the full resource picture is not yet complete. A 638-metre from-surface result confirms La Verde is growing toward the scale threshold that justifies advanced engineering studies.

headline: ABEN GOLD OPENS 2026 YUKON PROGRAM WITH 7.6m AT 3.66 g/t Au AT JUSTIN — Four POW Zone Holes Still Pending
snippet: Aben Gold (TSX-V: ABM) reported the first assay from its 2026 drill program at the Justin Gold Project in Yukon, with the opening hole returning 7.6 metres grading 3.66 g/t gold at the POW Zone — high-grade by Yukon exploration standards. Four additional POW Zone holes remain pending, meaning this release is a first read on a program that could deliver substantially more. For investors tracking Yukon gold explorers, the POW Zone result adds to the thesis that Justin hosts a continuous high-grade corridor with multi-hole reproducibility.

headline: CITI CUTS LITHIUM PRICE FORECAST 40% TO $12,000/T — Bank Sees Surplus Persisting Through 2028 as Demand Revisions Mount
snippet: Citigroup has slashed its lithium carbonate price forecast by approximately 40% to $12,000 per tonne — down from $20,000 — and cut its lithium hydroxide forecast to $12,000 from $17,000, citing downward demand revisions and a widening surplus the bank now expects to persist through the end of 2028. The cut arrives the same week SQM posted a Q3 earnings beat on record lithium volumes, illustrating the tension between current strong physical demand and the structural long-term glut Citi argues is building. For junior lithium developers, a Citi-endorsed $12,000/t floor raises serious questions about project economics at assets not yet in production.

headline: FULCRUM METALS LOGS 0.42% U3O8 SURFACE GRADES AT CHARLOT-NEELY — Athabasca Basin Margin Target Now Drill-Ready
snippet: Fulcrum Metals (LSE: FMET) reported surface uranium samples returning up to 0.42% U₃O₈ at its Charlot-Neely property in Saskatchewan's Athabasca Basin margin — results the company describes as fully defining its drill targets ahead of a maiden drill program. The 0.42% U₃O₈ surface grade is among the highest rock-chip results in the basin margin for a pre-drill stage company, distinguishing target quality from the more common low-grade surface anomalies that characterise first-pass uranium programs in the jurisdiction.

headline: CERRADO GOLD TAKES OVER PAN AMERICAN'S SHUTTERED PATAGONIA SILVER MINE — Argentine Past-Producer Back From 3-Year Care-and-Maintenance
snippet: Cerrado Gold has signed a purchase agreement to acquire a shuttered gold and silver mine in Patagonia from Pan American Silver — a past-producing operation on care and maintenance since early 2023. The deal includes a restart plan that positions the asset for near-term production at a point in the cycle where acquiring permitted brownfield infrastructure is significantly cheaper than developing greenfield. The transaction signals renewed operator confidence in Patagonian jurisdiction and precious metals economics at a time most of the sector is in defensive mode.

headline: DISTRICT METALS LOGS HIGH-GRADE URANIUM SURFACE SAMPLES IN NORTHERN SWEDEN — Ardnasvarre Targets Europe's Under-Explored Uranium Belt
snippet: District Metals (TSX-V) reported high-grade uranium surface samples from its Ardnasvarre property in northern Sweden — a jurisdiction with minimal modern uranium exploration despite regional geology that parallels more intensively explored Scandinavian uranium belts. The company identified additional targets beyond the initial sample sites, suggesting the property is part of a larger mineralizing system. Sweden's strategic position in the EU's domestic battery supply chain gives uranium exploration there a policy tailwind that most Canadian or Australian programs lack.

headline: COPPER'S 15.6% 2026 GAIN TEETERS AS SELLOFF DEEPENS — Averin: Supercycle Thesis Intact But Requires Rate Pivot to Re-Activate
snippet: Commodity strategist Ruslan Averin's November 2026 commentary argues that copper's year-to-date gain of 15.6% — holding well ahead of crude oil's 7.6% decline amid Iran talks — reflects genuine supply fundamentals that have not been invalidated by this week's financial market selling. Averin frames the current selloff as a macro overlay event rather than a copper-specific demand crisis, distinguishing between the financial market price and the physical market reality described by Asia Copper Week delegates. His thesis: the supercycle narrative survives the November correction but requires a Fed pivot catalyst to re-activate the equity-side of the trade.

headline: FED HIKE PROBABILITY HITS 92% AS GOLD BREAKS $3,800 — USAGold: Dollar at 19-Month High, No Support Until $3,700
snippet: USAGold's November 18 daily precious metals report frames gold's break below $3,800 as a direct consequence of surging December Fed hike probability — now priced at approximately 92% — pushing the dollar to 19-month highs and squeezing out leveraged Comex long positions. The analysis identifies no meaningful technical support between current levels and $3,700, arguing the gold-dollar relationship has entered a phase where the traditional portfolio hedge function of gold is temporarily overridden by the carry cost of holding non-yielding assets in a rising-rate environment. This dynamic typically reverses when rate expectations peak — but timing depends on data, not the calendar.
